cost: not exposed; no separate API/OCR calls made

findings.boundary: One clear merged/missing distinct question boundary: printed Q3 on PDF p.330 was not separately extracted and appears within an oversized Q2 record. Other sampled transcribed question boundaries were identifiable; continuations were generally distinguishable.
findings.native_stratum: On sampled native pages, question detection was generally strong. Noted Q19 option D split into two options and footer/page contamination in options on p.178 and p.305. Q26 p.449 has a possible spelling discrepancy (‘civile’ visually vs ‘civilie’ extracted); retain for human check.
findings.ocr_stratum: Scanned pages show substantial option-level OCR problems: missing options in Q6 p.339 and Q61-Q63 p.414, option-label duplication in Q23 p.405 and Q62 p.414, garbled/reordered option text on p.405, and extraction noise from answer marks on p.339.
findings.reviewer_uncertainty: Blind transcription has a possible normalization/error: p.405 Q21 option 1 was recorded ‘Video-conferencing’; source image appears to print ‘Vedio-conferencing’. Frozen blind file is unchanged; count this as reviewer transcription uncertainty, not extraction error. Case names and noisy scan glyphs remain unverified.
findings.denominators: 8 sampled pages inspected (including all pages in the frozen sample); 14 complete questions transcribed under the first-two-per-page rule; 1/14 clear boundary mismatch. Four additional visible questions were incomplete/outside transcription scope. Option issues are qualitative observations, not an exhaustive error rate. No CER or corpus error rate calculated.

caveats: AI visual observations are not human ground truth.
The sample is small, stratified by extraction method, and should not be used to estimate corpus-wide error rates.
No legal answers or source text were inferred or corrected.
Page-level visual count includes continuation and cutoff questions as noted in comparison.json.
